newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club negotiating for Denver accord on Russia.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club negotiating for Denver accord on Russia.

text.p: The Paris Club is hoping to reach agreement by next month paving the way for Russia's entry to the creditor nations grouping, though technical problems remain to be resolved, its chairman said on Wednesday.
The United States is seen as keen to be able to announce Russia's entry to the Paris Club at a Group of Seven rich nations summit it will host in Denver next month to be attended by Russia.
Paris Club chairman Christian Noyer told reporters that negotiations were under way with Moscow and would continue ahead of the Denver summit.

"The different parties (involved in the negotiations) hope to be able to resolve this question, at least on the major principles, before Denver," he said. "All technical questions have not been resolved to date."
Entry to the Paris Club would open the way for negotiations on debt owed by former allies of the old Soviet Union in African and Latin America.
But the Paris Club has yet to resolve how to treat that debt, and apply to it an appropriate modern day exchange rate. Most of the debt was taken out in roubles many years ago.
Noyer said the interests of the debtor countries involved would have to be taken into account before any deal on bringing Russia into the Paris Club was finalised.
Russia is seeking entry to the Paris Club along with other international organisations, including the World Trade Organisation, as quickly as possible.

G7 finance ministers and central bankers, bolstering Russia's bid for Paris Club membership, said last month that they "look forward to an agreement that would permit Russia to participate in the Paris Club as a creditor on appropriate terms."
Diplomats had said Russia's entry to the Paris Club depended primarily on a political decision which would create a climate to overcome remaining technical problems.
Noyer said however there were both political and technical issues to be resolved, and said he would hold further talks with Russia before the Denver summit to try to deal with these.
